Telr and CreditPool Partner to Launch Telr Multi-Card Payments, First in MENA
summary:
Telr, a regulated regional payments provider with acquiring and payment capabilities across key Middle Eastern markets, has partnered with CreditPool to introduce Telr Multi-Card Payments, a first-of-its-kind service in the region, now available exclusively on Telr payment pages.
This pioneering feature lets customers split a single purchase across multiple cards, helping them overcome individual card limits and turning potential payment declines into successful transactions. For merchants, the service offers opportunities to increase sales, boost average order values, and reduce cart abandonment, while giving customers the added benefit of combining rewards from different cards.
Khalil Alami, Founder and CEO of Telr, commented: “Telr continues to pioneer payment innovation, and we are extremely proud to have partnered with CreditPool to introduce such a sophisticated payment solution, marking another first in the MENA region. We are excited to launch this groundbreaking service. Telr is a fintech-forward acquirer, redefining payments through innovation and security, and a trusted growth partner for every merchant. We won’t accept anything less.” Alami added: “It is with great pleasure that we launch this first-of-its-kind payment service as a result of our partnership with CreditPool. We are solving the number one reason for payment declines: insufficient funds, and turning declines into approvals to unlock limitless purchasing power and transform ambition into boundless success through Telr Multi-Card Payments and our full suite of services, as we continue towards a sophisticated, fully digital economy.”
Rafik Ibrahim, Co-Founder and CEO of CreditPool, commented:
“At CreditPool, we believe every shopper should have the freedom to complete the purchases that matter to them, without the constraints of single-card limits. Telr’s trusted payments expertise makes them the right partner to help deliver a seamless and secure multi-card payment experience. This launch brings a new level of flexibility to the payment experience, helping merchants capture more revenue while improving the customer journey.”
Telr goes beyond payments with a comprehensive suite of e-commerce solutions, including social commerce, invoicing, Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), and financing. Backed by the UAE Central Bank’s Retail Payment Services License, the launch of Telr Multi-Card Payments reinforces Telr’s position as a fintech pioneer, delivering secure, seamless, and future-ready solutions that support business growth across MENA.

title: Bank With Ambition: LHV Bank Joins PRA and FCA Scale-up Unit to Accelerate UK Growth
summary:
LHV Bank has joined the second cohort of the PRA and FCA’s Scale-up Unit, strengthening its plans to grow its UK banking businesses and support the next generation of financial services innovation.
The Scale-up Unit was launched in October 2025 as part of the Government’s Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy. It provides high-growth banks and building societies with dedicated regulatory engagement to help them scale sustainably and responsibly.
For LHV Bank, the move marks the next chapter in its UK growth story, building on full UK banking authorisation in 2023 and strong momentum across retail banking, SME lending and Banking Services.
Built to scale. Banking with ambition.
LHV Bank has grown across three complementary businesses: an app-based retail current account bank for savers who take their money seriously; flexible lending for ambitious UK businesses; and Banking Services, providing the accounts, payments infrastructure and technology that fintechs and financial institutions rely on to serve their customers across the UK and Europe.
The bank’s growth is reflected in its 2025 results, with £1.1bn in customer deposits, £0.7bn in lending and £5m profit after tax.
Its Banking Services business also gives LHV Bank a distinctive role in the financial services ecosystem, powering other businesses with the infrastructure they need to innovate, grow and reach more customers. 
Supporting the next stage of growth.
Through the Scale-up Unit, LHV Bank will benefit from a dedicated regulatory contact who understands its business model and growth ambitions. This will support more tailored engagement on product development, regulatory processes and the practical challenges of scaling a modern banking business.
Kris Brewster, Interim Chief Executive Officer of LHV Bank, said:
“We’re ambitious about what LHV Bank can achieve in the UK. Joining the Scale-up Unit is an important step in our growth story and supports our commitment to scaling responsibly, with the right governance, resilience and customer focus.
“Our ambition is simple: to make banking work harder for our customers and partners. That means competitive savings products for people who take their money seriously, lending that helps ambitious businesses grow, and building the payment infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions across the UK and Europe depend on.
“We’re proud to be building a bank with ambition, and we look forward to working closely with the PRA and FCA as we continue to grow and contribute to the UK’s financial services sector.”

Travelex Canada Onboards More Than 50 Wholesale Customers in First Year of Trading
summary:
Leading foreign exchange company Travelex has onboarded more than 50 wholesale customers in Canada during its first year of trading in the region, as it targets further expansion across the country’s foreign exchange and financial services sectors.
Since launching its Canadian wholesale operation in October 2025, Travelex has built a customer base spanning foreign exchange operators and money services businesses (MSBs) across Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia. During this time, the business has traded 56 currencies, while providing customers with access to around 80 currencies through Travelex’s extensive global network.
Travelex has also established relationships with major liquidity and currency supply partners including Bank of America and Scotiabank, while leveraging its own global supply network to source currencies from markets including the UK, Singapore and the UAE.
Demand has largely been driven by Canadian outbound travel, including both holidaymakers and expatriate communities travelling overseas, while increased inbound travel to Canada during 2026 has created additional opportunities across both the buying and selling of foreign currency.
“Welcoming more than 50 customers in our first year demonstrates both the strength of demand and the significant potential of Canada’s wholesale foreign exchange market.
“Our success has been built on combining strong local relationships with the scale, expertise and supply capabilities of Travelex’s global network. This allows us to give customers access to a broad range of currencies, backed by the service and reliability they expect from a leading wholesale partner,” said Davish Bucktowar, Wholesale Trading Director at Travelex.
As it enters its next phase of growth in Canada, Travelex has also begun rolling out TravelNet, its proprietary self-service ordering platform, to customers across the market. Sitting alongside existing dealing channels including phone and email, TravelNet gives customers greater control over foreign currency ordering and pricing while providing a faster and more efficient digital ordering experience.
“We are excited to continue growing our MSB customer base while building new relationships with credit unions, financial institutions and banknote wholesale customers across the country.
“TravelNet will be an important part of that growth, giving our partners greater control over their ordering while we continue to invest in our supply chain and expand the services we can offer,” Bucktowar added.
Claire Shen, Manager, Currency Mart Inc. said:
“TravelNet has made managing our foreign currency requirements significantly easier. The platform is intuitive, convenient, and simple to use, allowing our team to place orders quickly and efficiently.
Having real-time access to rates and a streamlined ordering process has improved our day-to-day operations and enhanced the overall customer experience. TravelNet has become a valuable tool for our business, and we appreciate the reliability and support provided by the Travelex team.”

Financial Providers Are Ready for Agentic AI Onboarding, but Consumers Aren't
summary:
Financial services providers are preparing for a future in which AI agents open accounts on behalf of customers, but consumers are far from ready to hand over control. New research from Signicat, the European leader in digital identity and fraud prevention solutions, finds that 65% of consumers welcome AI assistance with financial applications, provided they retain control over decisions.
The Battle to Onboard 2026: The AI Reality Check, explores the attitudes, behaviours and perceptions around digital identity, verification and online trust of both consumers and financial service providers (FSPs) across Europe as we enter the agentic AI era. It also examines the state of digital onboarding today, finding that 60% of European consumers have abandoned an online financial application, compared with 68% in Signicat’s 2022 report.
“It is startling that years of digital investment have not significantly lowered the percentage of abandoned online applications,” said Dr Leda Glyptis, Board Chair at Bourn AI. “That means as an industry we are not listening to consumers properly, nor understanding their red lines. This gap, where we haven’t listened enough up until yesterday, is where today’s opportunity lies.”
Key findings include:
Onboarding issues persist: 60% of consumers report abandoning an online financial application in the last year. Although down from 68% four years ago, consumers cite the same problems, such as excessive information requests and lengthy processes.
Identity is a ‘red line’ for AI onboarding: Only 15% would trust AI to use their digital identity to verify who they are to the bank, and 14% would trust AI to sign contracts on their behalf to open an account.
Provider readiness for AI is running well ahead of consumer acceptance: 79% of providers are prepared for AI-initiated applications, while just 14% of consumers are comfortable with AI opening a financial product on their behalf.
Consumers are using AI but trust is highly dependent on risk: When asked what tasks they would trust AI with, most cited recipe creation (42%) or drafting emails (38%). Only 8% would be happy with AI making high-value purchases on their behalf, and 19% would let AI make smaller purchases.
Today consumers want a copilot, not an autopilot: While 65% prefer AI to assist with financial applications, from providing information to preparing applications for approval, only 11% want AI to complete the application on their behalf.
Financial providers have a significant trust advantage: Consumers are almost twice as likely to trust financial providers (44%) than AI providers (23%) to keep their personal data safe, potentially giving FSPs an advantage in AI-driven finance.
The research also found that digitally advanced markets are not necessarily those most willing to embrace an agentic AI future. Despite Norway leading Europe in digital ID preference, it is the market least comfortable with AI opening a financial product on a consumer's behalf (79% not comfortable). Finland (78%) and Sweden (73%) follow a similar pattern. 69% of UK consumers are not comfortable with AI opening a financial product on their behalf.
“The gap between provider expectations and consumer comfort with AI is an issue that financial services have faced many times before, from online banking to contactless payments,” said Emma Bauer, CPO at Signicat. “The rise of chatbots has also shown us that AI adoption can scale dramatically. How quickly it happens, and which providers are best positioned to benefit, will hinge on building trust and ensuring that people, businesses and AI agents can interact securely and with confidence. That means preparing now, with measures such as real-time fraud prevention and Know Your Agent frameworks.”

Axiology Partners With VIALET to Bring Tokenised Money Market Funds to Client Safeguarding
summary:
Axiology, a regulated European capital markets infrastructure provider, has partnered with Lithuanian electronic money institution VIALET to enable the use of tokenised money market funds (MMFs) for client fund safeguarding and corporate treasury management. 
VIALET, which manages approximately €150 million in assets and processes €6 billion in gross payment volume over the trailing twelve months, currently safeguards client funds through credit institution accounts and investment-grade government bonds. Through Axiology's infrastructure, VIALET will gain access to eligible tokenised MMFs, allowing it to diversify exposure beyond individual banks while improving liquidity management and creating opportunities to earn a return on the asset holdings. 
The partnership comes as tokenised money market funds gain traction in institutional finance. According to the European Central Bank, the global market for tokenised MMFs grew by approximately 110% in 2025, reaching around €7 billion by February 2026. The growth reflects increasing interest in using tokenisation to improve access to short-term investment instruments and liquidity management. 
The partnership addresses a key challenge for electronic money institutions (EMIs), balancing asset quality and diversification with immediate access to liquidity. With e-commerce operating around the clock and payment providers facing strict daily settlement deadlines, standard MMF redemption cut-offs can present challenges for safeguarding, regardless of whether fund units are tokenised. Axiology addresses this through a separate arrangement with an eligible liquidity provider, enabling access to cash intraday without changing the underlying funds' redemption terms. This helps reduce operational friction while supporting the liquidity requirements of payment businesses. 
Marius Jurgilas, CEO of Axiology, said "For payment institutions, safeguarding is not just about asset quality, funds must also be accessible when payments need to be settled. By pairing regulated money market instruments with intraday liquidity provider under one roof, institutions can diversify their safeguarding arrangements without adding unnecessary operational complexity." 
The collaboration demonstrates how tokenisation can support practical financial operations beyond traditional securities markets. Axiology operates a regulated DLT Trading and Settlement System under the EU DLT Pilot Regime, providing VIALET with access to digital securities infrastructure operating within Lithuania's regulatory framework. 
Mantas Staliūnas, CEO of VIALET, said, “We set four non-negotiable requirements: same-day liquidity, high asset quality, regulatory clarity and lean operations. Axiology met all four. As a Vilnius-headquartered electronic money institution, we also want to build with Lithuanian innovators and foster the fintech ecosystem we belong to.”

title: Transaction Network Services (TNS) Helps Businesses Increase Payment Acceptance With Smart Routing
summary:
Transaction Network Services (TNS) has enhanced its Payment Orchestration platform with smart routing capabilities that help businesses improve payment performance, optimize transaction costs and maintain greater control over how payments are processed. Designed for unattended and high-volume payment environments, the solution helps operators across parking, EV charging, transportation, vending, retail and other industries route transactions based on business rules, performance signals and provider availability to help maximize approval rates and reduce payment complexity.
Payment optimization is critical in today’s complex landscape where no two transactions are identical. The issuer, acquirer, card type, payment method, transaction channel and geography all affect whether a transaction is approved and at what cost. For operators processing high transaction volumes across multiple markets, even marginal improvements in acceptance rates and transaction costs can deliver significant commercial impact.
"Every failed transaction in an unattended environment represents lost revenue with no opportunity for recovery," said Michael Johnson, Global Managing Director, TNS Payments Market. "TNS’s optimal routing technology gives operators the intelligence to maximize the value of every payment by responding automatically to changing transaction conditions, helping to improve revenue without increasing operational complexity."
TNS’s Payment Orchestration platform helps reduce the operational burden often associated with managing payment performance across providers, channels, and markets. Smart routing automatically evaluates each transaction against configurable business rules, performance signals, and provider availability. It then directs the payment through the route best aligned with the operator’s priorities. The process runs continuously, reducing the need for manual oversight.
In addition, through the TNSPay Merchant Portal, businesses gain real-time visibility into payment performance across providers, channels, and locations. AI-assisted insights help operators identify trends, understand approval and decline patterns, and uncover opportunities that could help improve performance. With configurable dashboards, scheduled reporting, and the ability to explore payment data using natural language, teams can move from reporting on payment activity to making more informed optimization decisions.
"Every payment has an optimal path, but identifying and acting on that path in real time across hundreds of parameters is not something operators should have to manage themselves," said David Hore, Senior Director, Payments Product Portfolio, TNS Payments Market. "TNS Payment Orchestration uses smart routing to apply those parameters at scale, giving operators greater control over their routing strategy while removing the need to make individual transaction decisions manually.”  
Smart routing is part of TNS’s Payment Orchestration platform, which also supports TNS's Android-based unattended terminal portfolio and Bring Your Own App capabilities.

Planet and YouLend Partner to Bring Flexible Funding to European Businesses
summary:
Planet, a global provider of payments and software for retail and hospitality, has partnered with embedded financing platform YouLend to help small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Europe access working capital when they need it most.
Launching first in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Germany and Denmark, the partnership will make YouLend’s digital funding service available to Planet’s existing merchants through its established payments and property management software relationships.
Traditional lending can take weeks or months, and application success rates may not reflect seasonal trading patterns or the circumstances of companies with limited credit histories. Embedded finance offers a more responsive approach, using current business performance data to help SMEs access funding when they need it most.
YouLend manages underwriting, funding and servicing, while Planet connects eligible merchants to the service through the channels they already use. The digital application and assessment process can deliver a decision within minutes or hours, with funding typically available within 24 to 48 hours. Repayments are linked to a merchant’s sales, and the total cost is agreed and disclosed in advance, allowing hospitality, travel and retail companies to manage seasonal fluctuations without the cost increasing when revenue slows.
Since launching in 2017, YouLend has provided funding to over 400,000 businesses across 10 markets. Its data-led model can widen access to finance for smaller operators that conventional credit models may overlook, as well as for established SMEs.
“Businesses need quick, straightforward access to funding so they can act when opportunities arise,” said Planet’s Chief Commercial Officer Colin Close. “By bringing YouLend’s flexible finance into Planet’s existing services, we can help customers invest in their businesses, manage seasonal pressures and grow with greater confidence.”
The agreement brings business finance alongside the payments and operational software Planet already provides to hospitality, retail and travel merchants. It gives merchants a clearer route to support within an existing relationship.
“Partnering with Planet allows us to bring flexible funding to more merchants through the platforms and services they already use,” said YouLend’s Head of Strategic Partnerships Luuk Visschedijk. “By combining Planet’s established customer relationships and sector expertise with our data-led approach to funding, we can make access to working capital simpler and more convenient. It’s a great example of how embedded finance can help SMEs access the financial tools they need, when they need them.”
The move reflects a wider shift in financial services, as payments companies and software platforms bring funding closer to the merchants they already support. Planet and YouLend plan to widen access through Planet’s customer channels, giving more SMEs across other European markets a route to funding when they are ready to invest, adapt or grow.
YouLend retains responsibility for all funding decisions, pricing and terms, and Planet does not provide financial advice.

Backbase Introduces Delivery Factory to Accelerate Agentic Banking Implementations
summary:
Backbase today introduced Delivery Factory, an AI software factory purpose-built for banking, in which a bank's delivery team works alongside specialist AI agents from the first agreed requirement to working code. Across more than 10 Backbase implementations over the past 12 months, teams using it delivered twice as fast as traditional teams and 30% faster than teams working with generic AI coding assistants.
A generic coding assistant starts from the code in front of it. Delivery Factory starts from what the bank has agreed. Scoping documents, architecture specifications and meeting notes are combined with Backbase's own product knowledge into one shared project context, and every person and every agent on the team works from it, through design, planning, implementation and review. Requirements stop being re-specified at each handoff, and decisions made in a workshop carry through to the code.
The same implementations reported 80% less effort on requirements and specifications, 40% less coding and review effort, and a 60% increase in test and automation coverage.
Each role on the team has an agent to work with. Business analysts use the Business Analyst Agent to turn the project context into specifications, user stories and acceptance criteria, which become Jira work items. Solution architects use the Solution Architect Agent to weigh design decisions, find reusable services and produce architecture for review. Backend, Mobile and Web Agents prepare implementation plans grounded in the project's requirements and the bank's Backbase version. Engineers take the reviewed plans into their own coding tools and inspect every code change and verification result before work moves forward, while delivery leads coordinate scope, decisions and planning. The team directs the work throughout, and implementation runs through the bank's connected repositories, development environments and delivery pipelines.
Greg Fahy, CTO Digital Banking at Backbase: “Delivering banking software takes a whole team. Business analysts, solution architects, delivery leads and engineers need to stay aligned as a customer requirement becomes a working experience. Delivery Factory gives them and their AI agents a shared foundation: what the bank has agreed on, how its project is designed and how Backbase works. That helps teams spend less time reconstructing context and more time delivering the changes their customers need.”
Backbase is also introducing two agents that extend Delivery Factory across the platform lifecycle. The Backbase Migration Agent helps teams bring existing journeys, integrations and business logic to the Banking OS, adapting what a bank already has instead of rebuilding it from scratch. The Backbase Upgrade Agent helps existing customers keep their Backbase platform current, applying platform changes and flagging what needs attention, so upgrades become part of ongoing delivery rather than a separate project.

OMS Integrates With Keychain
summary:
One Mortgage System (OMS), the CRM and loan origination platform for intermediaries and lenders, has added Keychain to its growing range of CRM integrations, providing OMS users with access to faster digital client onboarding and AI-powered document analysis technology.
Keychain enables brokers to manage a range of early-stage client tasks, including digital fact finds, medical questionnaires, secure document collection and e-signing. Its AI-powered technology can analyse and verify documents, identify missing information and flag potential issues, helping brokers address gaps before a case progresses. Automated reminders can also be used to prompt clients for outstanding information.
The integration has been developed closely with existing OMS and Keychain clients, with more than 600 live mortgage, protection and specialist finance cases flowing from Keychain into OMS over the last few months.
As part of the integration, Keychain will offer OMS users an extended free trial period, allowing firms to assess how the technology works within their own business before deciding whether to continue with the service.
OMS and Keychain will also host a joint webinar on the 10th November to demonstrate the new functionality and explore the practical use of AI within the mortgage process. 
OMS is the UK’s only end-to-end platform covering residential, buy-to-let, second charge, equity release, bridging, and commercial mortgages - plus general insurance, and protection - to provide users with best in class for product sourcing, protection sourcing and criteria searching.
Jodie Andrews, Head of Sales, Marketing & Partnerships at One Mortgage System, commented:
“A modern CRM should be doing far more than simply managing client and case information. Brokers increasingly need access to specialist tools at different stages of the mortgage process, but that shouldn’t mean adding more keying and more complexity.
“Our focus is on extending what brokers can access through OMS by working with providers that solve specific problems. Keychain is a good example of that approach, bringing AI-powered document analysis and client onboarding into the wider OMS environment and giving brokers more ways to save time, improve efficiency and focus on growing their business.”
Jack Rogers, co-founder of Keychain, commented:
“OMS has a strong focus on bringing the best tools together in one place through integrations. We’re delighted to integrate with a business that shares our view that technology should make advisers’ lives easier and improve the experience for clients.
“Keychain is a specialist platform for client onboarding, covering everything from fact finding and document collection to AI-powered document analysis. The integration means firms can use those capabilities while information flows directly into OMS. We’ve already seen from mutual clients how much time this can save advisers and administrators, and we’re excited to make that experience available to more OMS users.”
Liz Syms, CEO of Connect for Intermediaries, an OMS and Keychain client, commented:
“Client onboarding is where most of the time goes at the start of a case. Since we introduced Keychain, clients complete their fact find and upload documents in a few clicks, the automated reminders do the chasing, and our advisers and administrators are no longer asking for the same information twice. That has given the team back hours every week to spend on advice rather than admin.
“The integration with OMS removes the step nobody enjoyed, which was keying the same client details into a second system. Cases and documents now flow straight through into OMS, so the information is captured once. Across a network of our size that is a significant saving on every case, and it also takes away the errors that creep in when data is re-typed.

As merchants grow and expand into new markets, their payment needs become more demanding. Supporting higher transaction volumes, different customer preferences and market-specific requirements calls for a payment infrastructure that can scale with the business.
This is particularly important for larger merchants, which increasingly need payment partners that can support complex requirements across markets. The right technology, payment expertise, dedicated human support and infrastructure can help merchants improve payment performance, scale effectively and support long-term growth, an approach that is central to emerchantpay’s proposition.
emerchantpay’s payment solutions have received industry recognition, with the company named Fintech of the Year at The Brit Fintech Awards 2026. It has also secured two wins at The FinTech Awards 2026, in the categories of Best FinTech for Personal Banking, Personal Payments and Money Management and Best FinTech for Hospitality and Catering. Additionally, emerchantpay has been shortlisted for Best Digital Solution Provider PayTech and UK PayTech of the Year at The Banking Tech Awards 2026.
Alexander Berrai, Deputy CEO at emerchantpay, comments:  “These results show that merchants want more from their payments partner. Checkout performance now has a direct impact on sales and customer retention, so merchants are choosing partners who can help them grow, not just process payments.
